Class EntryStubGenerator

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.build.EntryStubGenerator
public final class EntryStubGenerator extends Object
Generates the class that lets the launcher start the application through an interface call.

The class it writes is this, give or take the constant pool:

package io.micronaut.runner.generated;

public final class AppEntry implements io.micronaut.runner.Entry {
    static {
        io.micronaut.runner.Launcher.register(new AppEntry());
    }

    public void run(String[] args) throws Throwable {
        com.example.Application.main(args);
    }
}

It is packaged as an ordinary application class, so the launcher's Class.forName on it runs the static initialiser, which hands the launcher an instance, on which the launcher calls Entry.run(String[]). Entering the application is then an invokeinterface followed by an invokestatic: neither java.lang.reflect nor java.lang.invoke is pulled onto the startup path, and no method handle bootstrap is paid for. run declares Throwable so that whatever the application throws travels out of the launcher unchanged.

Class file version

The version is set explicitly to 69.0 (Java 25, the baseline of this project). ClassFile otherwise defaults to the version of the JDK that happens to run the packager, so packaging on a newer JDK would produce a class that the JDK 25 running the application cannot load - a failure at startup, in the artifact, that the build would never see.

Eligibility

A stub that cannot work is worse than no stub at all: it fails when the application starts rather than when it is packaged, and the launcher's reflective fallback would have started the same application without complaint. ineligibilityReason(String, byte[]) is therefore deliberately narrow, and it answers by parsing the main class rather than loading it - a packager must never run application code or initialise application classes.

Since:
1.0

  • Method Details

    • generate

      public static byte[] generate(String mainClass)
      Generates the entry stub for an application.

      The caller is expected to have found ineligibilityReason(String, byte[]) to be null first; this method assumes the main class is one the generated code may call.

      Parameters:
      mainClass - the binary name of the application main class, for example com.example.Application
      Returns:
      the class file of "io.micronaut.runner.generated.AppEntry"
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name is not a legal binary class name
      NullPointerException - if the name is null

    • ineligibilityReason

      public static String ineligibilityReason(String mainClass, byte[] classFile)
      Decides whether an application can be entered through a generated stub, by parsing its main class.

      Eligible means: the class file really is the class it was looked up as, it is a public class (not an interface, not abstract), it is not in the default package, and it declares itself - not inherits - a public static void main(String[]). That is exactly the shape for which an invokestatic behaves like the main method selection of the java launcher, which the runner's reflective fallback reproduces: the fallback prefers the String[] form over the no-argument form throughout the hierarchy and accepts instance methods, so any other shape has to keep using it.

      Parameters:
      mainClass - the binary name of the application main class
      classFile - the bytes of that class, as they are packaged; they are parsed, never loaded
      Returns:
      null when a stub can be generated, otherwise why it cannot, phrased to be read after "no entry stub was generated because ..."
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
